blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: "The only access was the UVC."
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: You describe there -- there you describe it's pulled back to ensure the inferior vena cava rather than the portal vein is the only available venous access and you talk about the drugs that were administered. Then you talk about talking to the family. That's a summary, isn't it, of what is about a three-page statement to the coroner for a formal inquiry? Do you make reference in the course of that statement to the rash you described with the colouring patches, the flitting patches, and something that didn't fit with anything you'd ever seen before?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: No, I haven't. And --
blocks.speaker: JAYARAM

blocks.text: Given what you've said -- sorry.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: And I can explain that because when I do a coroner's statement, it has to be factual, it has to be based on what I'd written in the notes. I can't do a coroner's statement (inaudible) something else in and at that time again -- and I can't remember exactly when I looked up "air embolism" and found that paper. You may have the date there. I presume it was before writing this statement from what you're saying.
blocks.speaker: JAYARAM

blocks.text: In a Coroner's Court, as my learned friend absolutely says, it's to establish cause of death and, if there isn't, should there be
blocks.speaker: JAYARAM

blocks.text: anything else. And my concluding remarks to the coroner when I gave evidence were that I could not explain how this had happened. It wasn't my job there to say, "I think it could have been this". My job is to say I couldn't explain it and that's what I said because at that time I had no evidence, I had no reason, apart from association, to say, "I think there could have been an air embolism".
blocks.speaker: JAYARAM

blocks.text: Certainly there was a discolouration.
blocks.speaker: JAYARAM

blocks.text: So the statement to the coroner contains things that are not in your notes, doesn't it, Dr Jayaram?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: I beg your pardon?
blocks.speaker: JAYARAM

blocks.text: Your statement to the coroner does contain --
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JAYARAM

blocks.text: -- things that aren't in your notes.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: For example, the UVC. But I remember --
blocks.speaker: JAYARAM

blocks.text: So, for example, pulling back the UVC?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JAYARAM

blocks.text: So when you tell the jury you don't put in a statement to the coroner anything that isn't in the notes, that's not right, is it?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: I accept that.
blocks.speaker: JAYARAM

blocks.text: Yes. Now, the coroner wants to know what cause of death is; yes?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JAYARAM

blocks.text: And you've told us all in some detail here what your views were in all of that, haven't you?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: I've told you what I think it wasn't.
blocks.speaker: JAYARAM

blocks.text: Yes. And you've told us all about the discussions with your colleagues because you really wanted to understand what had taken place and you know very well that the description of a rash that occupied the place in your witness statement that it did, that you had never seen before, was plainly relevant if that was a detail you could give. Do you agree, it would be plainly relevant to the coroner?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: In retrospect, absolutely.
blocks.speaker: JAYARAM

blocks.text: In retrospect? Are you seriously suggesting that this is not relevant to a coroner:
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: "Unusual discolouration, flitting patches of pink areas on a background of blue/grey skin, appearing to appear and disappear, like a rash with meningococcal sepsis, which is caused by blood vessels bursting, flitting, reappearing, disappearing, didn't fit with anything I'd seen before, described the marks as blotches, which were fairly ill-defined, about 1 to 2 centimetres, not discretely round, but blotchy patches of brighter pinkness on a background of bluey/grey."
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: You didn't think that was relevant to tell the coroner; is that what you're saying?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: At that time one of the reasons I didn't put it into the statement was, as I said, it wasn't in the notes and unlike sort of pulling back the UVC, which I remembered at the time I wrote this statement, it wasn't there, and although I -- and I still wasn't aware of the clinical relevance. I'd had some ideas. It's not my job to be the coroner. It's my job to explain that I couldn't explain what was going on.
blocks.speaker: JAYARAM

blocks.text: You give the coroner the physical findings and observations that you made at the time and could make at the time, don't you?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JAYARAM

blocks.text: Yes. And then the coroner decides what's made of that.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: That's correct, isn't it?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: That's correct.
blocks.speaker: JAYARAM

blocks.text: Now, you first spoke to the police about this in June 2017, didn't you? That's when you were first interviewed by the police as a witness about these events?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JAYARAM

blocks.text: Certainly by the time you spoke to the police, you'd read what's in the paper, hadn't you?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JAYARAM

blocks.text: The research paper?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JAYARAM

blocks.text: And, as we've seen, you were able to give the police a description by that point of a rash on a bluey/grey background with bright pinkness; yes? I'd just like to put up the paper that you looked at, one page from it, page 24946.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: If we could just enlarge, please, there's a section that's been highlighted -- this is in the paper. We may see the again in the course of the case, but let's just put in this section because this is a section that has a description I'd like to ask you about. This is where it describes in the paper that you later read colouring that is said to in certain circumstances be associated in the paper with air embolus and it describes this:
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: "Blanching and migrating areas of cutaneous pallor were noted in several cases and one of our own cases we noted bright pink vessels against a generally cyanosed..."
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Cynaosed is blue, isn't it?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: It is, yes.
blocks.speaker: JAYARAM

blocks.text: "... cutaneous background."
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: So the paper, Dr Jayaram, the paper that you read at some point mentions moving patches of skin colour, doesn't it? The paper mentions bright pink against a blue background, doesn't it?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: It does.
blocks.speaker: JAYARAM

blocks.text: Yes. What you said to the police when you went to make your statement in 2017 was made after you had read this paper, wasn't it?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: It was.
blocks.speaker: JAYARAM

blocks.text: When you were interviewed?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JAYARAM

blocks.text: And you told the police about bright pinkness on a background of blue/grey, yes?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JAYARAM

blocks.text: You didn't mention bright pinkness on a background of blue/grey in your notes at the time, did you?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: I didn't at the time --
blocks.speaker: JAYARAM

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: -- because I wasn't aware of the clinical significance.
blocks.speaker: JAYARAM

blocks.text: And you didn't mention bright pinkness on a background of blue/grey when you made your statement to the coroner, did you?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: No, I didn't.
blocks.speaker: JAYARAM

blocks.text: Has your description of what you said to the police and you say now been influenced by what you read in that paper, Dr Jayaram?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: I would say it hasn't. And the reason being, as I say, it is very easy to have confirmation bias. I remember reading this paper for the very first time and reading about this description and really feeling quite cold and worried.
blocks.speaker: JAYARAM

blocks.text: Now, it is a matter of regret for me that I didn't mention this to the coroner in the statements or at the time. At the time, and I think I -- I can't remember the date of the coroner's inquest, I don't know if you have when it happened. I know it was quite a long time after I did the statement.
blocks.speaker: JAYARAM

blocks.text: I'm sure we can find out what it is.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Because that would be really helpful.
blocks.speaker: JAYARAM

blocks.text: Well, tell us what it is you want to say about it, please.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Well, the reason is at the time of the coroner's inquest -- and I can't remember quite when it was -- we as a group of clinicians had already begun to raise concern to members of the more senior management team in the hospital about the association that we'd seen with an individual being present in these situations and we at that time were -- how do I say this diplomatically? -- being told that really we shouldn't be saying such things and not to make a fuss. It's more complicated than that, but essentially.
blocks.speaker: JAYARAM

blocks.text: So I think at the time of the inquest, my concern -- and it is a matter of regret that I didn't mention these -- is that had I suggested this and this could have been happening, I didn't really have any hard evidence apart from the association that we'd seen, and it's a matter of regret, I wish I'd been more courageous at that time.
blocks.speaker: JAYARAM

blocks.text: There's absolutely nothing preventing you reporting to a coroner visual signs, as you've described to this jury, if you saw them, is there?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: There isn't.
blocks.speaker: JAYARAM

blocks.text: No. And nothing about those visual signs and reporting, let's remind ourselves, the shifting pink against a blue background that didn't fit with anything you'd seen before. It's a straightforward clinical observation isn't it?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: It is.
blocks.speaker: JAYARAM

blocks.text: And you didn't report it. So can I just be clear and can you help us? Has the description you read in that paper influenced what you're saying to the police and to us about the colours you now say you saw?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: No. Absolutely not. Categorically.
blocks.speaker: JAYARAM

blocks.text: My Lord, there will be other matters to deal with with Dr Jayaram in due course.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Not at this stage.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Dr Jayaram will be coming back.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: You'll be coming back again. I'm just going to see if there are any more questions at this stage.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: No, thank you, my Lord. Does my Lord have any questions at this stage?
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: I don't. Thank you very much.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: Certainly.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: That completes your evidence at this stage for today and at this stage, so you don't have to come back tomorrow, but you will have to come back later in the trial as I think you knew in any event.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Yes.

blocks.text: It is of vital importance -- and this is said to every witness who doesn't complete their evidence -- that you do not speak to anyone about this case or any of the questions you've been asked or the evidence you've given in relation to them in particular -- that applies to anyone, you shouldn't talk
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: to anyone about it, but in particular, obviously, to anyone who's a witness in this case.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Absolutely.
blocks.speaker: JAYARAM

blocks.text: That's of critical importance.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Yes, fully understood.
blocks.speaker: JAYARAM

blocks.text: Thank you very much indeed.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: I'm going to try to get some antibiotics this evening.
blocks.speaker: JUROR

blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Right. Thank you very much. Of course, remember your obligations as jurors and responsibilities. No research and no conversation with anyone who's not a fellow juror and when you're all together so that everyone can hear what's being said. Thank you very much indeed.
